behaviour: C1: EpochResolver AWAITS onApplicationMessage({rumor, data, senderPubkey}) for every application-message ingest result in all three ingest loops (processEvent, flushFutureBuffer, rollbackAndReplay), while marmot-ts's generator is suspended at its yield — so the journal put resolves before the library emits the message and before it saves the advanced MLS state. A guard comment at the yield consumer states the guarantee.
C2: A failing (rejecting, throwing, undeserializable) onApplicationMessage is warned and swallowed; it never aborts the ingest generator (the state save still runs).

C3: rumorJournal.ts: idb-keyval store few-rumor-journal, key `${groupId}:${rumorId}`, value {groupId, rumorId, senderPubkey, data, receivedAt}; putRumor idempotent, ackRumor deletes, listPendingRumors(groupId) FIFO by receivedAt, sweep by age (30 days) and per-group cap (1000, = dispatcher LRU cap).
C4: welcomeSubscription.subscribeToGroupMessages wires onApplicationMessage to the journal put for its group.

C5: Dispatcher acks (journal.ack) at the end of the queued block after all matching handlers, even when a handler throws. Not yet started when disposed: NOT acked — replays next session. Once fan-out has started it is acked in `finally` (at-most-once) even if disposal cuts it short. A sender-mismatched rumor is never acked; a duplicate is acked on the queue, never before the original's handlers finished. Ack failures are warned, never break the queue. On re-subscribe MarmotContext awaits the previous subscription's drain() (bounded) before reading the journal.

C6: subscription.replay(entries) feeds entries through the identical listener (choke point, LRU, handlers); MarmotContext calls it after dispatcher subscribe and before subscribeToGroupMessages, so replayed rumors run first and suppress live duplicates; drain() covers them.
C7: The journal is not part of the relay backup payload; it is cleared by clearAllGroupData (account-scoped clear) and per group on leave (leaveGroupImpl purge).
C8: Privacy invariant untouched: local-only storage, no new network publishes.
non_goals: Making dispatcher handlers idempotent (at-most-once semantics unchanged).
Hardening the existing id-based dedup against forged rumor ids (pre-existing, same key space as the LRU).
